quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing your lane but there is no crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the pedestrian, then pass them.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane, even without a marked crosswalk. Pedestrians have the right-of-way.

questions.question: You just had an argument and feel angry. What should you do before driving?

options.text: Play loud music on the radio to distract yourself.
Wait a few minutes until you calm down.
Drive on the interstate to release your anger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes until you calm down.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your driving ability. You need to be calm and focused before driving. Take time to settle down before you get behind the wheel.

questions.question: Which is unlawful?

options.text: Passing another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Passing another vehicle at a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass in no passing zones or at railroad crossings. You also cannot pass on hills, curves, or where you cannot see far ahead. Do not pass at street crossings, work zones, or when a solid yellow line is next to your lane.

questions.question: Your vehicle breaks down on an interstate highway. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn to get other drivers' attention.
Get out and flag down the next vehicle.
Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay inside your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay inside your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle if you can. Standing on the highway is dangerous because vehicles travel at very high speeds.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear bumper):

options.text: Can frustrate and anger other drivers.
Will not result in a traffic ticket.
Helps prevent being cut off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can frustrate and anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is unsafe and can lead to aggressive driving. You may receive a traffic citation for unsafe driving.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
Drive at your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down in work zones and follow posted speed limits. Workers may be present. Be alert and prepared to stop at any time.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Signal your intention.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal before moving. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look at your blind spots. These actions alert other drivers and help prevent collisions.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Saves time.
Helps you avoid obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury or death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury or death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. Speeding does not save time and leads to dangerous driving decisions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hospital.
Intersection ahead.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you an intersection is coming. Prepare to stop, turn, or watch for traffic.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right and you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus.
Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn.
questions.explanation: Never try to fit your vehicle between a turning truck or bus and the curb. You could be hit. Wait for the truck or bus to finish turning before you turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that you cannot turn in the direction of the arrow. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look to your:

options.text: Left, right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left, then right, then left again before entering an intersection. Check for cars or pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from the left side will be closer to you.

questions.question: On a slippery road, you should keep a following distance that is:

options.text: The same as normal.
Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, your car takes longer to stop. Keep extra distance between your car and the car ahead.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let another driver take over.
Drink something with caffeine.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let another driver take over.
questions.explanation: Stop driving if you feel tired. Take a break every hour on long trips. Share driving with another person when possible.

questions.question: Drivers aged 16 or 17 cannot use:

options.text: A cell phone.
A text messaging device.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers aged 16 or 17 cannot use any cell phone or mobile device while driving, including hands-free devices. Breaking this rule can result in license suspension.

questions.question: Which statement is true about changing lanes?

options.text: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Cars with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder. This helps you see vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles in your blind spot.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses after the "Don't Walk" signal starts flashing. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:

options.text: Proceed because you have the right-of-way.
Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians finish crossing before you proceed. You must yield to pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: The crossing is controlled. Continue at your regular speed.
Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: When you see this sign near railroad tracks, slow down and look and listen for trains. Be ready to stop and let any trains pass.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian crossing your lane with no crosswalk, you should:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
Carefully drive around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross, even if there is no marked crosswalk. Pedestrians have the right-of-way in the roadway.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop at an intersection.
When there is a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a red traffic light. You must also obey police officers directing traffic, regardless of any signs or signals.

questions.question: To make a left turn, you should:

options.text: Turn from the rightmost lane.
Turn from the leftmost lane.
Turn from any lane if you signal ahead of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn from the leftmost lane.
questions.explanation: Turn from the lane closest to where you want to go. Turn into the lane closest to the one you left. This way, you cross fewer lanes of traffic.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
You do not need to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first. Once the intersection is clear and the signal allows, you can complete your turn.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right to cross at crosswalks. You must stop for them, whether the crosswalk is marked or not.

questions.question: In a vehicle with airbags, where should children age 12 and under sit?

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pickup truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Airbags can be dangerous for children. Anyone age 12 or under must sit in the back seat.

questions.question: When taking medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor how it affects driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor how it affects driving.
questions.explanation: Any medicine—prescription or over-the-counter—can affect your driving. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before driving to learn if a medicine will impair you.
